title: Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt
capsule: The Twenty-third Dynasty was a line of Libyan (Meshwesh) pharaohs who ruled concurrently with, and in opposition to, the Twenty-second Dynasty during Egypt's Third Intermediate Period, from roughly 837 to 735 BCE by some reckonings. Founded at Leontopolis in the Delta by Pedubast I, the dynasty held sway over parts of Upper Egypt and competed for legitimacy with Tanis-based rulers, producing a fragmented polity in which multiple kings sometimes reigned simultaneously. The dynasty's kings — including Iuput I, Shoshenq IV, and Osorkon III — appear principally in temple donation stelae and priestly records rather than military annals. The dynasty was absorbed into the broader collapse of Libyan rule when Kushite kings of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty consolidated control over all Egypt by c. 715 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the dynasty's reach at any given moment depended on local priestly and military alliances rather than clear administrative boundaries, and Egyptologists differ on both the dynastic sequence and dates.
